title: Customer identification programme for banks
text: A bank must implement a written Customer Identification Programme that includes risk-based procedures to verify the identity of each customer before opening an account, and must retain the identifying information used.

title: Beneficial ownership requirements for legal entity customers
text: A covered financial institution must establish and maintain written procedures reasonably designed to identify and verify beneficial owners of legal entity customers at the time a new account is opened.

title: Reports of suspicious transactions
text: A bank shall file a suspicious activity report no later than 30 calendar days after the date of initial detection of facts that may constitute a basis for filing, and shall not notify any person involved that a report was filed.

title: Blocked property and rejected transaction reporting
text: Any person holding blocked property must report to OFAC within 10 business days of blocking, and must file an annual report of blocked property held as of 30 June each year.

title: Error resolution procedures for electronic fund transfers
text: A financial institution shall investigate promptly and determine whether an error occurred within 10 business days of receiving a notice of error, and shall report the results to the consumer within three business days of completing the investigation.

title: Record retention under Regulation B
text: For 25 months after the date that a creditor notifies an applicant of action taken on an application or of incompleteness, the creditor shall retain in original form or a copy thereof any application that it receives and any written or recorded information used in evaluating the application.

title: Heightened standards for risk governance frameworks
text: A covered bank should establish and adhere to a written risk governance framework that includes independent risk management and internal audit, with the board providing active oversight and credible challenge of management.

title: Third-party relationships: interagency risk management guidance
text: A banking organisation should conduct due diligence before entering a third-party relationship, maintain written contracts addressing performance and audit rights, and conduct ongoing monitoring proportionate to criticality.

title: Cybersecurity risk management, strategy and governance disclosure
text: A registrant must describe its processes for assessing, identifying and managing material risks from cybersecurity threats, and must disclose board oversight and management expertise in annual reports.

title: Safeguards Rule: elements of an information security programme
text: A financial institution shall designate a qualified individual to oversee its information security programme, conduct written risk assessments, implement access controls and encryption, and report to the board at least annually.

title: HIPAA administrative safeguards
text: A covered entity must implement policies and procedures to prevent, detect, contain and correct security violations, including risk analysis, workforce sanctions, and periodic evaluation of security measures.

title: Compliance programme requirement
text: Every reporting entity shall implement a compliance programme that includes the appointment of a compliance officer, written policies and procedures, a risk assessment, ongoing training and a biennial effectiveness review.

title: Suspicious transaction reporting timing
text: A reporting entity shall send a suspicious transaction report as soon as practicable after it has taken measures that enable it to establish there are reasonable grounds to suspect a transaction is related to money laundering.

title: Third-party risk management
text: A federally regulated financial institution should maintain a third-party risk management framework with a centralised record of arrangements, risk-based due diligence, contractual rights to audit, and exit and transition plans for critical arrangements.

title: Technology and cyber risk management
text: An institution should maintain a technology and cyber risk management framework covering governance, risk management, technology operations, cyber security, and third-party provider oversight, with reporting to senior management.

title: Operational resilience and operational risk management
text: An institution should identify critical operations, set tolerances for disruption, conduct scenario testing against severe but plausible scenarios, and maintain a resilience framework approved by senior management.

title: Complaint handling procedures for banks
text: A bank shall establish procedures for dealing with complaints, designate an officer responsible, deal with a complaint within 56 days of receipt, and inform the complainant of the external complaints body.

title: Financial crime systems and controls
text: A firm must ensure that its systems and controls enable it to identify, assess, monitor and manage money laundering risk, and that they are comprehensive and proportionate to the nature, scale and complexity of its activities.

title: Customer due diligence measures
text: A relevant person must identify the customer and verify their identity on the basis of documents or information obtained from a reliable source, and where there is a beneficial owner, take reasonable measures to verify their identity.

title: Consumer Duty: acting to deliver good outcomes for retail customers
text: A firm must act to deliver good outcomes for retail customers across products and services, price and value, consumer understanding and consumer support, and must monitor and evidence outcomes on an ongoing basis.

title: Operational resilience: important business services
text: A firm must identify its important business services, set impact tolerances for each, carry out mapping and scenario testing, and remain within impact tolerance for each important business service in the event of a severe but plausible disruption.

title: Outsourcing and critical third parties
text: A firm must exercise due skill, care and diligence when entering into, managing or terminating an outsourcing arrangement, and must ensure the arrangement does not impair the quality of its internal control.

title: COREP and FINREP regulatory returns
text: A firm must submit prudential returns covering own funds, liquidity and large exposures at the frequency and within the remittance dates set out in the reporting rules, and must have adequate controls over data quality.

title: Security of processing
text: The controller and processor shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk, including pseudonymisation and encryption, and a process for regularly testing effectiveness.

title: Notification of a personal data breach to the regulator
text: In the case of a personal data breach, the controller shall without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after having become aware of it, notify the supervisory authority unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk.

title: Senior management responsibilities and accountability
text: A firm must allocate prescribed responsibilities to senior managers, maintain responsibilities maps and statements of responsibility, and certify annually that certified staff remain fit and proper.

title: Records of processing activities
text: Each controller shall maintain a record of processing activities under its responsibility containing the purposes of processing, categories of data subjects and personal data, recipients, transfers and retention periods.

title: Data protection impact assessment
text: Where processing is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller shall, prior to processing, carry out an assessment of the impact of the envisaged processing operations.

title: ICT risk management framework and governance
text: Financial entities shall have in place an internal governance and control framework that ensures effective and prudent management of ICT risk, with the management body bearing ultimate responsibility and approving the ICT strategy.

title: Reporting of major ICT-related incidents
text: Financial entities shall report major ICT-related incidents to the competent authority using harmonised templates, submitting an initial notification, an intermediate report and a final report within the prescribed deadlines.

title: Own funds requirements and capital ratios
text: Institutions shall at all times satisfy a common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4.5 percent, a tier 1 capital ratio of 6 percent and a total capital ratio of 8 percent of the total risk exposure amount.

title: Strong customer authentication for electronic payments
text: A payment service provider shall apply strong customer authentication where the payer accesses a payment account online, initiates an electronic payment transaction or carries out any action through a remote channel implying risk of fraud.

title: Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction
text: Regulated entities shall undertake customer due diligence while commencing an account-based relationship, obtain officially valid documents, carry out risk categorisation of customers and conduct periodic updation of KYC records.

title: Storage of payment system data
text: All system providers shall ensure that the entire data relating to payment systems operated by them is stored in a system only in India, and shall submit a system audit report conducted by a CERT-In empanelled auditor.

title: Master Direction on Information Technology Governance, Risk and Controls
text: Regulated entities shall put in place a board-approved IT strategy and policy, constitute an IT strategy committee, maintain an information security policy and conduct periodic vulnerability assessment and penetration testing.

title: Master Direction on Outsourcing of Information Technology Services
text: Regulated entities shall not outsource core management functions, shall conduct due diligence on service providers, include audit and inspection rights in agreements, and maintain exit strategies for material outsourcing.

title: Internal Ombudsman and complaint redressal
text: Regulated entities shall appoint an Internal Ombudsman to examine complaints that are partly or wholly rejected, and shall display the grievance redressal mechanism prominently at branches and on the website.

title: Cyber security and cyber resilience framework for regulated entities
text: Regulated entities shall adopt the cyber security and cyber resilience framework covering governance, identification of critical assets, protection, detection, response and recovery, with periodic reporting to the board.

title: Obligations of a data fiduciary
text: A data fiduciary shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures, protect personal data in its possession, and intimate each affected data principal and the Board in the event of a personal data breach.

title: Fair practices code for lenders and digital lending
text: Regulated entities shall provide a key fact statement to the borrower before execution of the contract, disclose the all-inclusive annual percentage rate, and ensure recovery practices do not involve harassment.

title: Anti-money laundering obligations of financial institutions
text: Financial institutions shall establish customer identity identification systems, preserve customer identity materials and transaction records, and report large-value and suspicious transactions to the anti-money laundering authority.

title: Cross-border transfer of personal information
text: Where a personal information handler provides personal information outside the territory, it shall pass a security assessment organised by the state authority, obtain certification, or conclude standard contractual clauses.

title: Classified protection of important data
text: The state shall establish a classified and categorised data protection system; processors of important data shall designate a person responsible, conduct periodic risk assessments and report assessment results to the authorities.

title: Capital adequacy management for commercial banks
text: Commercial banks shall classify risk exposures under the prescribed tiers, maintain minimum capital adequacy ratios, and submit capital adequacy reports to the regulator on a quarterly basis.

title: Outsourcing risk management of information technology
text: Financial institutions shall assess the concentration risk of information technology outsourcing, retain ultimate responsibility for outsourced activities, and report material outsourcing arrangements to the regulator.

title: Risk-based approach to money laundering and terrorist financing
text: Financial institutions shall identify and assess money laundering risks across products, services, geographies and channels, apply risk-mitigating measures proportionate to assessed risk, and report the assessment to management.

title: Conduct of business rules for financial instruments business operators
text: A financial instruments business operator shall establish a system to ensure suitability of solicitation having regard to the knowledge, experience, financial position and investment purpose of the customer.

title: Reporting of personal data leakage
text: A personal information handling business operator shall report a leakage of personal data likely to harm the rights and interests of individuals to the Commission promptly, and notify the affected individuals.

title: System risk management and operational continuity
text: Financial institutions should develop contingency plans for system failures, conduct regular drills including joint drills with external providers, and report material system failures to the authority without delay.

title: Customer due diligence requirements
text: A financial institution shall identify the customer and verify the customer identity, identify any beneficial owner and take reasonable measures to verify the beneficial owner identity, before establishing a business relationship.

title: Risk-based approach and ongoing monitoring
text: An authorised institution should continuously monitor its business relationship with a customer, review existing records to ensure documents and information remain up to date and relevant, and scrutinise complex or unusually large transactions.

title: Operational resilience and operational risk management
text: An authorised institution should become operationally resilient by May 2026, identifying critical operations, setting tolerance for disruption, and conducting severe but plausible scenario testing with board oversight.

title: Outsourcing of activities by authorised institutions
text: An authorised institution should consult the regulator before entering into a material outsourcing arrangement, retain the ability to meet supervisory requirements, and ensure customer data confidentiality is maintained.

title: Security of personal data
text: All practicable steps shall be taken to ensure that personal data held by a data user is protected against unauthorised or accidental access, processing, erasure, loss or use, having regard to the harm that could result.

title: Internal controls and management responsibility
text: A licensed person should have internal control procedures and financial and operational capabilities which can reasonably be expected to protect its operations and its clients from financial loss arising from theft, fraud or other dishonest acts.

title: Safety and security of electronic financial transactions
text: A financial company shall comply with the standards for human resources, facilities, electronic devices and procedures necessary to ensure the safety and reliability of electronic financial transactions.

title: Duty of safety measures for personal information
text: A personal information controller shall take technical, administrative and physical measures necessary to secure safety, including establishing an internal management plan and keeping access records, to prevent loss or leakage.

title: Suspicious transaction and currency transaction reporting
text: A financial company shall report suspicious transactions to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit without delay, and report currency transactions exceeding the prescribed threshold within the statutory period.

title: Prevention of money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism for banks
text: A bank shall perform customer due diligence measures when establishing business relations, conduct enhanced due diligence on higher risk customers including politically exposed persons, and screen against relevant sanctions lists.

title: Cyber hygiene requirements
text: A relevant entity shall ensure administrative accounts are secured, security patches are applied in a timely manner, a baseline standard is implemented, networks are secured, malware protection is deployed and multi-factor authentication is enforced.

title: Risk management practices for outsourcing arrangements
text: An institution should maintain a register of all outsourcing arrangements, conduct due diligence and risk evaluation before outsourcing, and ensure the regulator has the right to access and inspect the service provider.

title: Cyber security governance and risk management
text: A member organisation shall define, approve and implement a cyber security governance structure, appoint a cyber security function independent of IT, and conduct periodic cyber security risk assessments reported to the board.

title: Anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing rules
text: A financial institution shall apply customer due diligence measures, maintain records for at least ten years, appoint a compliance officer at management level and report suspicious transactions to the Financial Intelligence Unit.

title: Business continuity management requirements
text: A member organisation shall maintain a business continuity management programme including business impact analysis, recovery time objectives for critical services, and annual testing of continuity and disaster recovery plans.

title: Risk management and internal controls for banks
text: A bank shall maintain a governance framework in which the board approves risk appetite, the risk and compliance functions have unrestricted access to the board, and internal audit independently assesses control effectiveness.

title: Risk management and compliance programme
text: An accountable institution must develop, document, maintain and implement a risk management and compliance programme setting out how it identifies, assesses, monitors, mitigates and manages money laundering risk.

title: Responsible business conduct and disclosure
text: A financial institution shall disclose all fees, charges and interest in a key facts statement before onboarding, resolve customer complaints within the prescribed timeline and maintain a complaints register.

title: Security measures on integrity and confidentiality of personal information
text: A responsible party must secure the integrity and confidentiality of personal information in its possession by taking appropriate, reasonable technical and organisational measures to prevent loss, damage or unauthorised access.
